stem: Phosphorus and chlorine are elements in Period 3 of the Periodic Table.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Chlorine forms three different compounds with phosphorus.

The most common compounds are $\text{PCl}_3$ and $\text{PCl}_5$.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
Complete Table 1.1.

Table 1.1

| compound | oxidation number of P | oxidation number of Cl |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $\text{PCl}_3$ |  |  |
| $\text{PCl}_5$ |  |  |

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
In a closed system, $\text{PCl}_3$ and $\text{PCl}_5$ exist in an equilibrium mixture as shown in reaction 1.

reaction 1 $$\text{PCl}_3\text{(l)} + \text{Cl}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{PCl}_5\text{(s)} \qquad \Delta H = -124\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

Deduce two conditions that favour the production of $\text{PCl}_5$ in reaction 1.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
The third compound of phosphorus and chlorine, $\mathbf{W}$, has a relative molecular mass, $M_{\text{r}}$, between that of $\text{PCl}_3$ and $\text{PCl}_5$. The compound contains 69.6% by mass of chlorine.

Determine the molecular formula of $\mathbf{W}$.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text:
$\mathbf{W}$ is a liquid at room temperature and pressure. It reacts vigorously with water to form an acidic solution.

Suggest the structure and bonding in $\mathbf{W}$. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Fig. 1.1 shows a reaction scheme involving $\text{P}_4$ and $\text{Cl}_2$.

parts.label: (b)(i)

parts.text: Write an equation for the formation of $\mathbf{A}$ in reaction 3.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Name $\mathbf{B}$, which is formed in both reactions 4 and 5.

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.text: Draw the structure of $\mathbf{C}$, used in reaction 6.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
1,2-dichloroethane, $\text{ClCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$, reacts with $\text{NaOH}$ to produce an unsaturated compound, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{Cl}$, as shown in reaction 7.

reaction 7 $$\text{ClCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{Cl} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{NaCl}$$

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: State what is meant by unsaturated.
